operational_specification.population: Training runs on UCI HAR subject-disjoint split with PreNormTransformerEncoder under SGD optimization
operational_specification.unit_of_analysis: One paired per-seed training run (intervention and comparator share seed ID)
operational_specification.intervention: Server-bound target blocks.0.fc1.weight has stored tensor shape (128, 64). Post-step spectral norm clipping on blocks.0.fc1.weight with threshold 5.0
operational_specification.comparator: Control arm, defined by what the harness guarantees rather than by a description of the intervention. Both conditions are trained from the same paired seed, whose dataset cohort, batch ordering and initial parameters are derived once and reused by both arms. Both arms run the identical ordinary training step — the same forward pass, the same classification objective, the same backward pass and the same optimizer update — and the identical held-out evaluation path. The harness invokes the registered lifecycle machinery in both arms, so the control arm reaches every registered point on the same inputs (post step). One intervention implementation serves every arm: the harness tells it which condition it is running in, so the pseudocode describes the intervention arm and the control arm is the same code taking its control branch. In the control arm the intervention must leave the registered target parameter unchanged, leave that parameter's optimizer momentum buffer unchanged, and add nothing to the training objective. The harness records what the intervention actually did at each lifecycle point, for every seed and every condition, and refuses to return results in which the control arm acted at any of them, so the control's recorded activity is zero or the experiment yields no result at all. Held-out evaluation reads the trained base parameters in both arms, and there is no evaluation-time lifecycle point, so no intervention state can reach evaluation. Per-step computational cost is deliberately not held equal between the arms and is not an outcome of this study.

pseudocode: Read target parameter tensor W with shape [128, 64] from harness
Read momentum_buffer m associated with W from harness (may be None)
Initialize vector u of shape [128] with values from dedicated random generator
Initialize vector v of shape [64] with values from dedicated random generator
For iteration in range(15): compute v = W.transpose(0,1) @ u
If spectral_norm > threshold: compute scale = threshold / spectral_norm
If spectral_norm > threshold: apply W.data.mul_(scale) in-place
If spectral_norm > threshold and m is not None: apply m.data.mul_(scale) in-place
Write modified W back to harness target parameter slot

Scope (server-owned): control arm. Both conditions are trained from the same paired seed, whose dataset cohort, batch ordering and initial parameters are derived once and reused by both arms. The harness invokes the registered lifecycle machinery in both arms, so the control arm reaches every registered point on the same inputs (post step). If the condition the harness passes in is a control condition, return here: add no term to the training objective, and leave the registered target parameter and that parameter's optimizer momentum buffer exactly as received. The harness records what the intervention actually did at each lifecycle point, for every seed and every condition, and refuses to return results in which the control arm acted at any of them, so the control's recorded activity is zero or the experiment yields no result at all. Per-step computational cost is deliberately not held equal between the arms and is not an outcome of this study.
intervention_protocol.application_timing: Executed lifecycle (server-owned): the operator is invoked after the optimizer step of every optimization step: the operator modifies the parameters or optimizer state the standard update just produced, so the modification persists into subsequent steps and into the evaluated weights.
intervention_protocol.tensor_axis_or_scope: Full weight matrix treated as linear operator from R^64 to R^128
intervention_protocol.ordering_rule: Power iteration order: v update then u update, repeated 15 times for convergence
intervention_protocol.normalization_rule: L2 normalization of u and v vectors after each power iteration step with epsilon 1e-10
intervention_protocol.numerical_safeguards: Epsilon 1e-10 added to all norm denominators; scale computation guarded by spectral_norm > threshold condition
invariants: Spectral norm of W after intervention is at most 5.0
Control arm leaves W and momentum_buffer bit-identical to pre-step state
Power iteration uses deterministic 15 iterations regardless of convergence
Momentum buffer scaled by same factor as W when clipping occurs

operational_specification.outcome_formula: number of correct activity predictions / 2947 windows in the official subject-disjoint UCI HAR test split
operational_specification.failure_handling: A non-finite outcome is never a data point: the harness raises on any non-finite value for either condition in that seed pair, so the job fails and reports nothing rather than a value it did not measure. No preregistered seed is discarded, skipped, or rerun, and no outcome is imputed.
operational_specification.smallest_worthwhile_effect_basis: Versioned policy accuracy_fraction_v1 in proportion: max(absolute floor 0.005, fixed SD multiplier).
operational_specification.planning_sd_basis: Immutable calibration record ef4188ff-a4a8-4720-a3a7-f59d889d0c94; baseline-only paired-null bootstrap UCL80 under recipe sha256:94f3ad0aa281d8b6845da79f0abcea1cd604a36c8b00ffcce5861e16cc4ff155.
operational_specification.decision_consequence: If supported for uci_har_small_transformer_v1 held-out classification accuracy: recommend testing spectral norm clipping on feed-forward layers as a regularization option for subject-disjoint time-series transformer training within this testbed scope. A positive result would justify testing whether the effect transfers to other subject-disjoint temporal datasets or transformer scales. If the preregistered primary contrast refutes the hypothesis, redirecting regularization efforts to attention mechanisms or input representations for uci_har_small_transformer_v1. If inconclusive: increase compute budget or test alternative spectral norm thresholds within this testbed before drawing conclusions about the mechanism.
operational_specification.mechanistic_rationale: Feed-forward layers in transformers apply non-linear transformations to attention outputs before residual addition. Unconstrained weight growth during training can increase the Lipschitz constant of these transformations, amplifying small input perturbations and reducing robustness to subject variability. Spectral norm clipping bounds the operator norm, limiting how much feature magnitudes can grow through the feed-forward transform. This should preserve signal-to-noise ratio across subjects with different movement patterns while maintaining capacity to learn discriminative temporal features.
alternative_hypotheses: Spectral norm clipping constrains representational capacity too severely, reducing training fit and harming generalization
Feed-forward layer stability is not the limiting factor for subject-disjoint generalization; attention or input layers dominate
SGD momentum already provides implicit regularization that makes explicit spectral constraints redundant
boundary_conditions: Results apply to transformer architectures with residual feed-forward layers on time-series classification tasks
Threshold value 5.0 selected for this architecture scale; different model sizes may require threshold tuning
Subject-disjoint evaluation specifically; random splits may show different effects
12-epoch training budget; longer training may change constraint effectiveness

Scope (server-owned): single calibrated testbed uci_har_small_transformer_v1 — UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones (DOI 10.24432/C54S4K; raw inertial signals, 128-timestep windows over 9 channels; official subject-disjoint split of 7,352 training and 2,947 held-out windows); model PreNormTransformerEncoder(Linear(9,64) + learned positional embedding(128,64); 2 blocks, each LayerNorm(64) -> 4-head self-attention over 128 timesteps with q/k/v/out Linear(64,64) -> residual -> LayerNorm(64) -> Linear(64,128) -> ReLU -> Linear(128,64) -> residual; final LayerNorm(64), mean-pool over time, Linear(64,6)); evaluated as the official UCI HAR test split — 2,947 windows recorded from 9 subjects who appear in no training window, so the held-out cohort is subject-disjoint rather than a random row split, and is never used for training or tuning
For each seed, both conditions use identical initialization, data split/order, stochastic draws, hyperparameters, tuning, update count, and compute budget.
Model and optimizer state are reset independently for each condition; no trained state is carried between paired runs.
negative_controls: Apply spectral norm estimation and scaling factor computation but multiply W by scale drawn from Uniform(0.95, 1.05) instead of threshold-based clipping, preserving compute path without the constraint direction
leakage_risks: Held-out test statistics must not influence preprocessing or training decisions
Random generator for power iteration must be dedicated and not shared with other stochastic operations
Momentum buffer modification must only occur when W is actually clipped to avoid control/intervention divergence
operational_specification.primary_outcome: held-out classification accuracy: number of correct activity predictions / 2947 windows in the official subject-disjoint UCI HAR test split; unit=proportion; range=[0, 1]; computed once per seeded run; higher is better; failure handling: A non-finite outcome is never a data point: the harness raises on any non-finite value for either condition in that seed pair, so the job fails and reports nothing rather than a value it did not measure. No preregistered seed is discarded, skipped, or rerun, and no outcome is imputed.
operational_specification.estimand: Hypothesis-positive paired contrast H_s = outcome_intervention - outcome_comparator; estimand = arithmetic mean of H_s over the preregistered primary seed IDs.
operational_specification.sample_size_rationale: Prospective paired normal approximation with two-sided alpha=0.05: planning SD(H_s)=0.0250196 proportion, worthwhile effect=0.0125098, target power=0.90, required n=43; fixed n=43. Planning-SD basis: Immutable calibration record ef4188ff-a4a8-4720-a3a7-f59d889d0c94; baseline-only paired-null bootstrap UCL80 under recipe sha256:94f3ad0aa281d8b6845da79f0abcea1cd604a36c8b00ffcce5861e16cc4ff155. Worthwhile-effect basis: Versioned policy accuracy_fraction_v1 in proportion: max(absolute floor 0.005, fixed SD multiplier).
operational_specification.decision_value: Using the two-sided paired-bootstrap 95% CI for mean(H_s), support the preregistered directional effect only when CI_low > 0.0125098; refute that directional effect when CI_high <= 0; otherwise report inconclusive. The paired sign-flip p-value is descriptive and does not replace this decision rule. Decision consequence: If supported for uci_har_small_transformer_v1 held-out classification accuracy: recommend testing spectral norm clipping on feed-forward layers as a regularization option for subject-disjoint time-series transformer training within this testbed scope. A positive result would justify testing whether the effect transfers to other subject-disjoint temporal datasets or transformer scales. If the preregistered primary contrast refutes the hypothesis, redirecting regularization efforts to attention mechanisms or input representations for uci_har_small_transformer_v1. If inconclusive: increase compute budget or test alternative spectral norm thresholds within this testbed before drawing conclusions about the mechanism.
falsification_criteria: Refute the preregistered directional effect when the two-sided paired-bootstrap 95% CI upper endpoint for mean(H_s) is <= 0.
Do not claim a worthwhile directional effect unless that CI's lower endpoint exceeds the fixed margin 0.0125098 proportion.
